studies.study_name: A Phase 1-2 Study of Weekly OGX-011 Plus a Gemcitabine/Platinum-Based Regimen in Patients With Stage IIIB or IV Non Small Cell Lung Cancer
studies.design: open-label, single-group (no comparator arm), multicentre phase 1/2 add-on study. ClinicalTrials.gov designInfo: allocation NA, interventionModel SINGLE_GROUP, masking NONE, primaryPurpose TREATMENT. Custirsen was added to a gemcitabine/platinum backbone in every subject, so no custirsen-free control exists within the trial.
studies.indication: stage IIIB or IV non-small cell lung cancer
studies.population: chemotherapy-naive advanced NSCLC; one group, 'OGX-011 - Intent to Treat Analysis Set' = all subjects who received at least one dose of OGX-011
studies.n_analyzed_platelet: 81 - the Intent to Treat Analysis Set that is the denominator of every posted platelet row (participantFlow STARTED 81; baseline denom 81; adverse-events eventGroup EG000 seriousNumAtRisk 81 and otherNumAtRisk 81). Do NOT use 85: the 4-subject gap between enrolment and the ITT set is never resolved in the record. Do NOT sum the four platelet rows - 'Platelet Count Decreased' (6/81, Investigations), non-serious 'Thrombocytopenia' (25/81, Blood and lymphatic), serious 'Thrombocytopenia' (1/81) and serious 'Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura' (1/81) are four overlapping views of the same 81 subjects.
studies.dose_regimen: custirsen 640 mg IV over 2 h on Days -7, -5 and -3 of Cycle 1 (loading doses), then 2-h infusions weekly on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 21-day cycle; with gemcitabine 1250 mg/m2 IV Days 1 and 8 and cisplatin or carboplatin IV Day 1. CAVEAT the dose is modal, not uniform: 'Most patients received OGX-011 at 640 mg; but 3 patients received a 480 mg dose. The 2 dose groups were combined due to the small number of patients who received 480 mg.' (adverse-events eventGroup EG000 description).
studies.duration: maximum 6 cycles of 21 days; AE observation window = 'treatment-emergent events in all subjects who had at least one adverse event with onset on or after the date of administration of the first dose of study treatment through 30 days after the last dose of study treatment' (adverseEventsModule.timeFrame)
studies.platelet_endpoint_basis: adverseEventsModule.description: "Adverse events are systematically assessed through regular investigator assessment and laboratory testing that is clearly defined in the protocol." Each platelet term carries assessmentType SYSTEMATIC_ASSESSMENT, and four platelet terms are tabulated with counts and denominators: otherEvents 'Platelet Count Decreased' (organSystem Investigations) 6/81; otherEvents 'Thrombocytopenia' (Blood and lymphatic system disorders) 25/81; seriousEvents 'Thrombocytopenia' 1/81; seriousEvents 'Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura' 1/81. Locus: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT00138658 -> resultsSection.adverseEventsModule, fetched 2026-10-01.
studies.verification_locus: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT00138658 fetched 2026-10-01: identificationModule.orgStudyIdInfo.id = 'OGX-011-05'; interventions = [DRUG 'custirsen sodium', otherNames ['OGX-011','TV-1011']]; phases ['PHASE1','PHASE2']; conditions ['Non-small Cell Lung Cancer']; enrollmentInfo {count 85, ACTUAL}; resultsFirstPostDateStruct 2012-01-10. All four curated platelet values were re-derived from the fetched resultsSection and match exactly: 6/81=7.4%, 25/81=30.9%, 1/81=1.2%, 1/81=1.2%.
studies.notes: ATTRIBUTION: not custirsen-attributable. Single-group design with gemcitabine plus cisplatin or carboplatin in every subject; gemcitabine and carboplatin are each independently thrombocytopenic and gemcitabine is a recognised cause of drug-induced thrombotic microangiopathy, which is the plausible alternative explanation for the single TTP case. The curated rows correctly set effect_vs_control to TBD. CURATION DEFECT (not corrected here, this file does not modify the input): rows TMSR503-TMSR506 carry exposure_duration '... after loading doses days -7,-5,3'. The '3' reproduces a typo in the registry's own armsInterventionsModule intervention description; the adverse-events eventGroup description in the same record reads 'Days -7, -5 and -3 of Cycle 1', which is the internally consistent reading. The published primary report is Laskin JJ et al., J Thorac Oncol 2012;7:579-86 (PMID 22198426) - the same trial, not a second evidence unit.

studies.study_name: A Pilot Study Evaluating the Safety and Feasibility of Custirsen (OGX-011) in Combination With Second Line Chemotherapy in Patients With Hormone Refractory Prostate Cancer (CUOG trial P-06c)
studies.design: randomised, open-label, parallel-group phase 2 pilot study with TWO ACTIVE CUSTIRSEN ARMS and no custirsen-free arm: 'OGX-011 / mitoxantrone/prednisone' (EXPERIMENTAL) and 'OGX-011/docetaxel/prednisone' (EXPERIMENTAL). Randomisation allocates the chemotherapy backbone, not the oligonucleotide, so the trial cannot estimate a custirsen effect on platelets.
studies.indication: metastatic castration-resistant (hormone-refractory) prostate cancer progressing during or after first-line docetaxel
studies.population: men with mCRPC previously treated with docetaxel; 23 randomised to the mitoxantrone backbone and 46 to the docetaxel backbone
studies.n_enrolled: 70 (ClinicalTrials.gov enrollmentInfo count 70, type ACTUAL). 69 reached baseline and treatment (participantFlow STARTED 23 + 46; baseline denoms 23, 46, Total 69); the 1-subject gap is not explained in the record.
studies.n_analyzed_platelet: 23 for the mitoxantrone arm (TMSR507) and 46 for the docetaxel arm (TMSR508), from adverse-events eventGroups EG000 seriousNumAtRisk 23 and EG001 seriousNumAtRisk 46. These are DISJOINT arm denominators of one trial; they may be reported separately but must never be pooled with, or added to, the 81 of NCT00138658.
studies.dose_regimen: oral prednisone 5 mg twice daily from Day -10 throughout; three 2-h IV custirsen 640 mg loading infusions in the loading-dose period (registry intervention description: 'Days -9 to -1'; the adverse-events eventGroup description of the same record states 'Day -7, -5 and -3 of cycle 1'), with ibuprofen 400 mg or acetaminophen 650 mg premedication during loading only; then custirsen 640 mg weekly on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 21-day cycle. Backbone: mitoxantrone 12 mg/m2 IV over 30 min Day 1 (EG000) or docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV over 60 min Day 1 (EG001).
studies.duration: 21-day cycles continued to completion of the final treatment cycle; the record states no AE observation window (adverseEventsModule.timeFrame is empty)
studies.platelet_endpoint_basis: Supports a measured zero for the SERIOUS band only. The posted Serious Adverse Events table is a complete tabulation (no frequency threshold) and is populated for both arms with 23 distinct terms including 'Death', 'Gastrointestinal Haemorrhage' (0/23, 1/46), 'Haematuria' and 'Febrile Neutropenia' (1/23, 1/46), and no thrombocytopenia or platelet term appears anywhere in it - so zero serious platelet events in 23 and in 46 subjects. It does NOT support a zero for the non-serious band: adverseEventsModule.frequencyThreshold = 5, so absence from the 67-term non-serious table establishes only <5% per arm (blood/investigations terms that did clear 5%: Anaemia 8/23 and 8/46, Neutropenia 2/23 and 4/46, Weight Decreased 6/23 and 8/46, Aspartate Aminotransferase Increased 2/23 and 0/46). Downgraded from 'yes' to 'partial' because this record, unlike NCT00138658, carries NO assessmentType on any event, an EMPTY adverseEventsModule.description and an EMPTY timeFrame, so there is no quotable evidence in any source I reached that platelet counts were systematically measured under a defined observation window. Locus: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT00327340 -> resultsSection.adverseEventsModule, fetched 2026-10-01.
studies.verification_locus: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT00327340 fetched 2026-10-01: orgStudyIdInfo.id = 'OGX-011-07'; interventions = [DRUG 'custirsen (OGX-011)/mitoxantrone', DRUG 'custirsen (OGX-011)/docetaxel', each otherNames ['custirsen','OGX-011','TV-1011']]; phases ['PHASE2']; allocation RANDOMIZED; conditions ['Prostate Cancer']; resultsFirstPostDateStruct 2012-08-29. Every per-arm count asserted in the two curated rows' notes was re-derived from the fetched resultsSection and matches exactly, and the absence of any platelet term from both the 23-term serious and the 67-term non-serious tables was confirmed by enumerating all 90 terms.
studies.notes: This is the trial published as Saad F, Hotte S, North S, et al., 'Randomized phase II trial of Custirsen (OGX-011) in combination with docetaxel or mitoxantrone as second-line therapy ... CUOG trial P-06c', Clin Cancer Res 2011;17:5765-73 (PMID 21788353) - one trial, one evidence unit, counted once. IMPORTANT NON-OVERLAP: this trial is NOT one of the three constituents of the custirsen meta-analysis in this cluster. In PMID 30732140 it is cited only in the Introduction as reference [19]; the three INCLUDED RCTs are references [20], [21] and [25] (SYNERGY, AFFINITY and Chi 2010), so the pooled odds ratio TMSR511 and the two zero rows TMSR507/TMSR508 carry no shared patients. ATTRIBUTION: both arms received custirsen, so effect_vs_control is correctly TBD; the grade-0 rows are 'no serious platelet event observed under custirsen plus a myelosuppressive backbone', not a demonstration that custirsen spares platelets.

studies.sponsor_protocol_id: I153 (NCIC CTG IND.153); secondary ids CAN-NCIC-IND153, ONCOGENEX-OGX-01-01, CDR0000269888
studies.study_name: A Phase I Study Of Combination Neoadjuvant Hormone Therapy And Weekly OGX-011 (Clusterin Antisense Oligonucleotide) Prior To Radical Prostatectomy In Patients With Localized Prostate Cancer
studies.design: open-label, single-group, dose-escalating phase 1 pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic study across six dose cohorts (40, 80, 160, 320, 480, 640 mg), with androgen blockade (buserelin + flutamide) and radical prostatectomy as the tissue endpoint. ClinicalTrials.gov designInfo: allocation NA, interventionModel SINGLE_GROUP, masking NONE.
studies.indication: localized prostate cancer with high-risk features (PSA >10 ng/mL, stage T3, or Gleason 7-10), candidates for radical prostatectomy
studies.population: 25 men with previously untreated localized high-risk prostate cancer, distributed across six dose cohorts
studies.n_enrolled: 25 (ClinicalTrials.gov enrollmentInfo count 25, type ACTUAL; corroborated by the primary abstract, 'Subjects (n = 25) with localized prostate cancer')
studies.n_analyzed_platelet: TBD - and this is a real denominator problem, not an omission. The only platelet statement available is dose-specific: 'For patients receiving the 640 mg dose, the most frequent adverse events included thrombocytopenia ...'. The size of the 640 mg cohort is NOT stated in the Higano 2013 review, in the Chi 2005 abstract, or in the registry record, and the JNCI full text is closed access (Unpaywall oa_status closed; Europe PMC has no PMCID). The platelet denominator is therefore an unstated subset of the 25, NOT 25. Any analysis that treats the curated 640 mg row as covering 25 patients is wrong.
studies.dose_regimen: custirsen by 2-h IV infusion on Days 1, 3 and 5, then weekly from Day 8 for four doses, in six dose cohorts of 40, 80, 160, 320, 480 and 640 mg, combined with androgen blockade (buserelin + flutamide) from Day 1; prostatectomy on Days 30-36 (Chi 2005 abstract) / within seven days of the final custirsen dose (Higano 2013). The curated row TMSR509 is scoped to the 640 mg cohort only.
studies.duration: approximately 4 weeks of dosing (Days 1-29) followed by prostatectomy on Days 30-36
studies.platelet_endpoint_basis: The platelet endpoint was assessed and graded, but no incidence and no denominator were published. Higano CS, OncoTargets Ther 2013;6:785-797, section 'Tolerability of custirsen', paragraph 1, citing reference 65 (Chi 2005): "In the first Phase I study of custirsen in prostate cancer, no dose-limiting toxicities were reported at the doses of custirsen investigated (up to 640 mg); all toxicities were grade 1/2 and typically occurred within the first week of administration. For patients receiving the 640 mg dose, the most frequent adverse events included thrombocytopenia, anemia, and leukopenia, and nonhematologic toxicities, such as fever, fatigue, rigors, and elevation of aspartate/alanine aminotransferase." Verified verbatim against the Europe PMC full text of PMC3699352 on 2026-10-01. Corroborated by the primary report's own abstract, Chi KN et al., J Natl Cancer Inst 2005;97:1287-96 (PMID 16145049): "Only grade 1 and 2 toxicities were observed." 'partial' not 'yes' because the severity band is bounded and thrombocytopenia is named as a most-frequent event, but no platelet count, no incidence and no evaluable denominator are reported anywhere I could reach.
studies.verification_locus: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT00054106 fetched 2026-10-01: officialTitle 'A Phase I Study Of Combination Neoadjuvant Hormone Therapy And Weekly OGX-011 (Clusterin Antisense Oligonucleotide) Prior To Radical Prostatectomy In Patients With Localized Prostate Cancer'; orgStudyIdInfo.id 'I153'; leadSponsor 'NCIC Clinical Trials Group'; phases ['PHASE1']; enrollmentInfo {count 25, ACTUAL}; start 2002-12-10, primary completion 2004-09-23; interventions [buserelin, custirsen sodium, flutamide, conventional surgery, neoadjuvant therapy]; resultsFirstPostDateStruct absent (no posted results). The identification of 'the first Phase I study of custirsen in prostate cancer' with this record is secured by three independent agreements: n=25, the 40-640 mg six-cohort range, and the neoadjuvant-hormone-plus-prostatectomy design, all of which appear in both the registry record and Higano's description of reference 65, and the Europe PMC record for PMID 16145049 confirms the JNCI 2005;97:1287-96 citation.
studies.notes: HIGHEST-ATTRIBUTION CUSTIRSEN PLATELET SIGNAL IN THIS CLUSTER, and the reason it matters is the absence of a myelosuppressive backbone: the co-medications are buserelin, flutamide and surgery, with no cytotoxic chemotherapy, unlike every other custirsen patient study here. That makes thrombocytopenia-as-most-frequent-AE at 640 mg the cleanest oligonucleotide-attributable platelet observation in the cluster - but it is qualitative only. Three evidence units converge on this one trial and it is counted ONCE: the registry record NCT00054106, the primary publication Chi KN et al. JNCI 2005 (PMID 16145049), and the Higano 2013 secondary report that is the curated source. CURATION DEFECT: row TMSR509 sets dose_or_conc_value 640 mg with no denominator field, so it silently implies the trial's n=25 applies to a statement that in fact applies only to the unstated 640 mg subcohort (see n_analyzed_platelet). LIMITATION: the JNCI per-dose toxicity table was not read.

studies.study_name: A single site, open label, two parallel group, one sequence (placebo followed by custirsen) crossover phase 1 study of two custirsen dosing regimens in healthy subjects (reported as Rabinovich-Guilatt L et al., Br J Clin Pharmacol 2015;80:436-45)
studies.design: single-site, open-label, two-parallel-group, one-sequence (placebo then custirsen) crossover phase 1 study; no formal randomisation - verbatim Methods: "This was a single site, open label, two parallel group, one sequence (placebo followed by custirsen) crossover phase 1 study." and "Subjects in the two groups were matched based on age (+/- 5 years) and weight (+/- 10 kg). No formal randomization was used." Each subject serves as his own placebo control on Day 1; the two groups are not compared statistically ("No formal statistical comparisons between treatment groups were performed").
studies.indication: none - healthy volunteers (clinical-pharmacology regimen-finding study to support a thorough QT study)
studies.population: 22 healthy subjects confined at the research centre, group A n=10 (premedication-only regimen) and group B n=12 (increasing-dose regimen)
studies.n_enrolled: 22 - verbatim: "Twenty-two subjects were enrolled and assigned to group A (n = 10) or B (n = 12)."
studies.n_analyzed_platelet: 22 assessed, 0 reported. All 22 had complete blood count with differential drawn at protocol-defined timepoints (see platelet_endpoint_basis), and the safety analysis in Table 1 covers all 10 + 12; but NO platelet count, platelet summary statistic or platelet adverse event is published, so the evaluable platelet denominator in the public record is zero. One group-B subject withdrew consent on day 6 after two custirsen doses and was excluded from the ECG endpoint analyses (11 of 12 completed), which does not affect the AE table.
studies.dose_regimen: custirsen 640 mg IV over 120 min in 250 mL normal saline, with dexamethasone 5 mg IV bolus 1 h before infusion. Group A: dexamethasone + placebo on Day 1, then dexamethasone + custirsen 640 mg on Day 8. Group B: placebo without premedication on Day 1, then custirsen 320 mg (Day 2), 480 mg (Day 4) and 640 mg (Day 6) with dexamethasone 5 mg (Day 2) and 3 mg (Days 4 and 6), then custirsen 640 mg on Day 8 WITHOUT premedication.
studies.duration: 8 dosing days plus a follow-up visit; haematology sampling window on Day 8 at 0 (pre-dose), 2, 12, 24, 36 and 48 h after the start of the custirsen infusion (plus Days 4 and 6 pre-dose in group B)
studies.platelet_endpoint_basis: Platelets were MEASURED under a defined exposure and a defined observation window, but no platelet result was reported. Assessment, verbatim Methods: "Laboratory evaluations included complete blood count with differential and coagulation studies (PT/PTT, INR) on day 8 at 0 (pre-dose), 2, 12, 24, 36 and 48 h after the start of the custirsen infusion (group A) and on days 4 and 6 at 0 (pre-dose) and on day 8 at 0 (pre-dose), 2, 12, 24, 36 and 48 h after the start of the custirsen infusion (group B)." A complete blood count with differential necessarily includes a platelet count, so the platelet endpoint was assessed at six post-dose timepoints at the full 640 mg clinical dose, graded per "National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events, version 4.0". Reporting: the words 'platelet' and 'thrombocytopenia' do not occur anywhere in the article (0 hits across the full rendered text of PMC4574829, checked 2026-10-01), while Table 1 does report a haematology adverse event, "Lymphocyte count decreased 1 (10) 1 (10) 0 0". So routine haematology was assessed and tabulated and no platelet event met the reporting bar - but per hard rule 5 that is NOT a measured negative platelet value, and no platelet-specific grade-0 row should be created from this paper. Locus: PMC4574829, Methods 'Assessments' and Table 1.
studies.verification_locus: Europe PMC EXT_ID:25782535 fetched 2026-10-01 -> PMID 25782535, PMCID PMC4574829, doi 10.1111/bcp.12633, Br J Clin Pharmacol 80 (2015), title 'Impact of dosing regimen of custirsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, on safety, tolerability and cardiac repolarization in healthy subjects.' Europe PMC fullTextXML is not served for this article (150-byte response), so the full text was read from the rendered article at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4574829/ and the Methods, Disposition and Table 1 passages quoted here were taken from it verbatim. REGISTRY SEARCH THAT FAILED, stated so it is not repeated: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 was queried for query.intr=custirsen (13 studies, all enumerated) and query.term=OGX-011 and query.term=TV-1011; the only healthyVolunteers=true custirsen record is NCT01874561 (TV1011-TQT-108, 'A Single-Center, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo- and Positive-Controlled, Parallel Group, Thorough QT/QTc Study ... in Healthy Men', n=155 ACTUAL, start 2013-05), which is a DIFFERENT and later study - the very thorough-QT study this regimen-finding study was run to enable. No registry identifier appears anywhere in the article ('NCT', 'registr' and 'ClinicalTrials' all absent from the full text).
studies.notes: registry_id and sponsor_protocol_id are TBD, NOT 'NOT_REGISTERED'. I could not find a registry record and the article carries none, but absence from the ClinicalTrials.gov searches above does not positively establish non-registration (the study is a Teva phase 1 healthy-subject study, a category outside FDAAA mandatory registration, and could sit in EudraCT or a national register I did not reach), so hard rule 1 requires TBD. WHY THIS UNIT IS WORTH KEEPING: it is the only custirsen exposure in humans in this cluster that is free of BOTH a cytotoxic chemotherapy backbone AND cancer, at the full 640 mg clinical dose. CURATION ENRICHMENT, row TMSR510 currently has readout_value TBD: the aPTT numbers ARE published, in Table 1 - 'Activated partial thromboplastin time prolonged' group A 9 (90) any grade and 6 (60) grade >=2, group B 11 (92) any grade and 1 (8) grade >=2 - alongside 'Six subjects (60%) in group A and three subjects (25%) in group B had at least one grade >=2 AE', 'All events considered related to treatment were grade 1 or 2', 'None of the AEs led to study discontinuation' and 'No serious AEs or deaths occurred'. The curated note's claim that the numeric table could not be retrieved is now superseded; the row's aPTT TBD is resolvable from Table 1. The curated row's grade-0 handling is otherwise sound and its is_platelet_specific=FALSE flag is correct, since aPTT is a coagulation and not a platelet endpoint. SIDE FINDING, no record created: the Introduction refers to 'a previous, unpublished work with custirsen in healthy subjects' in which ASO-induced AEs occurred despite NSAID premedication - an earlier healthy-volunteer study that is unidentifiable and unretrievable, so it is deliberately not instantiated.

studies.registry_id: NOT_APPLICABLE - a pooled analysis is not a trial and has no registry record. The three constituent trials carry NCT01188187, NCT01578655 and NCT00258388, each verified and recorded separately below.
studies.study_name: Meta-analysis of efficacy and safety of custirsen in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (Zhang X, Liu C, Li K, Wang K, Zhang Q, Cui Y. Medicine (Baltimore) 2019;98(6):e14254)
studies.design: aggregate-data meta-analysis of three randomised controlled trials, fixed-effects Mantel-Haenszel odds ratios for adverse events, no individual patient data. Comparison: 'Experimental, the group treated with docetaxel or cabazitaxel and prednisone plus custirsen; Control, the group treated with docetaxel or cabazitaxel and prednisone alone' (Fig 3 legend). NOT A TRIAL - it enrolled no one and measured no platelet count; it re-describes platelet events already counted inside its three constituents.
studies.phase: not_applicable (pools one phase 2 and two phase 3 trials)
studies.population: men with mCRPC receiving docetaxel or cabazitaxel plus prednisone, with or without custirsen
studies.n_enrolled: 1709 analysed across the three trials, 857 experimental and 852 control - verbatim: "The included 3 RCTs [20, 21, 25] represented 1709 participants (857 in the experimental group and 852 in the control group)." This is an ANALYSED total, not an enrolment total: the three trials enrolled 1022 + 630 (635 randomised per publication) + 82 = 1734 by registry counts.
studies.n_analyzed_platelet: 1709 (857 custirsen vs 852 control), and this number RECONCILES EXACTLY against the three constituents' safety analysis sets, which is the strongest check available on the pool's composition: SYNERGY safety set 501 + AFFINITY safety set 315 + Chi 2010 arm A 41 = 857, and SYNERGY 499 + AFFINITY 312 + Chi 2010 arm B 41 = 852. DO NOT add 1709 to any other denominator in this cluster, and do not add the constituents' own denominators on top of it - that would triple-count the same patients.
studies.route: intravenous (custirsen), with intravenous taxane and oral prednisone
studies.dose_regimen: custirsen 640 mg IV weekly after three 640 mg loading doses, added to docetaxel 75 mg/m2 q3w plus prednisone (SYNERGY, Chi 2010) or cabazitaxel 25 mg/m2 q3w plus prednisone (AFFINITY)
studies.duration: varies by constituent; not harmonised by the meta-analysis
studies.platelet_endpoint_basis: A platelet endpoint is explicitly pooled and reported with a comparator, twice, in Results section 3.3 and again in the Discussion: "it contains neutropenia (OR = 1.59, 95% CI = 1.28-1.98, P < .001), anemia (OR = 1.86, 95% CI = 1.50-2.31, P < .001), thrombocytopenia (OR = 2.62, 95% CI = 1.82-3.77, P < .001), and diarrhea (OR = 1.35, 95% CI = 1.11-1.63, P = .002)." The corresponding forest plot is "Figure 3 Forest plots showing changes in (A) OS, (B) neutropenia, (C) anemia, (D) thrombocytopenia, and (E) diarrhea." Inclusion required per-arm AE counts from every constituent: "the study should offer accurate date, including the total number of subjects, the OS, and the number of adverse events of each study group." Locus: Europe PMC full text of PMC6380863, Results 3.3 and Fig 3, fetched 2026-10-01. CAVEAT: Fig 3D is a raster image, so the PER-TRIAL thrombocytopenia event counts that produce the pooled OR could not be read.
studies.verification_locus: Europe PMC EXT_ID:30732140 fetched 2026-10-01 -> PMID 30732140, PMCID PMC6380863, doi 10.1097/MD.0000000000014254, Medicine 98 (2019), licence 'cc by-nc-nd'. The pooled thrombocytopenia OR 2.62 (95% CI 1.82-3.77, P<.001) asserted in row TMSR511 was re-read verbatim from the full text in two independent places. The three constituents are enumerated by the article itself as references [20], [21] and [25] and each was then verified against ClinicalTrials.gov and Europe PMC - see the three constituent records below.
studies.notes: ONLY CONTROLLED CUSTIRSEN PLATELET ESTIMATE IN THE CLUSTER, and the only one in which the comparator receives the identical myelosuppressive taxane backbone, so the OR isolates the custirsen increment rather than the chemotherapy's own thrombocytopenia. That makes it the single most useful platelet row here for causal attribution - and it is also the row most likely to be double-counted, because its 1709 patients sit inside three trials that are recorded separately. Treat the pool and its constituents as ONE body of evidence. constituents_identifiable is 'yes' on three independent grounds: the article names all three with full citations, each resolves to a verified ClinicalTrials.gov record, and the 857/852 split reproduces exactly from the three published safety analysis sets. CURATION DEFECT: row TMSR511's source_ref credits the article to 'Liu C, Li K.' The Europe PMC authorString is 'Zhang X, Liu C, Li K, Wang K, Zhang Q, Cui Y.' - the first author is Zhang X, and Liu C and Li K are the second and third authors. The PMID, PMCID, DOI, journal, year and e-locator in the curated source_ref are all correct; only the author attribution is wrong. NO OVERLAP with NCT00327340 in this same cluster: that trial is cited by this meta-analysis only in the Introduction as reference [19] and is not among the included studies.

studies.study_name: SYNERGY - A Randomized Phase 3 Study Comparing Standard First-Line Docetaxel/Prednisone to Docetaxel/Prednisone in Combination With Custirsen (OGX-011) in Men With Metastatic Castrate Resistant Prostate Cancer
studies.design: randomised (1:1, central, stratified by opioid use for cancer-related pain and radiographic evidence of progression), open-label, unmasked, parallel-group phase 3 trial at 134 centres in 12 countries; arms 'Custirsen, Docetaxel, Prednisone' (EXPERIMENTAL) and 'Docetaxel, Prednisone' (ACTIVE_COMPARATOR). This is the first of the three constituents that gives the pooled odds ratio a custirsen-free control arm.
studies.population: men with mCRPC and no previous chemotherapy, PSA >5 ng/mL, Karnofsky >=70%; 510 assigned custirsen/docetaxel/prednisone and 512 docetaxel/prednisone
studies.n_enrolled: 1022 (ClinicalTrials.gov enrollmentInfo count 1022, type ACTUAL; publication: "Between Dec 10, 2010, and Nov 7, 2012, 1022 patients were enrolled to the trial, of whom 510 were assigned docetaxel, prednisone, and custirsen and 512 were allocated docetaxel and prednisone.")
studies.n_analyzed_platelet: 501 custirsen vs 499 control - the safety analysis set, which is the denominator the meta-analysis used: "Patients who received at least one study dose were included in the safety analysis set" and "in the docetaxel, prednisone and custirsen group (n=501) compared with the docetaxel and prednisone alone group (n=499)". These 1000 subjects are INSIDE the pool's 1709; never add them to it.
studies.dose_regimen: docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV with prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily in both arms; the custirsen arm additionally received "weekly doses of custirsen 640 mg intravenously after three loading doses of 640 mg"
studies.duration: to progression or unacceptable toxicity; median overall survival 23.4 months vs 22.0 months
studies.platelet_endpoint_basis: Assessed and counted per arm, but the per-arm platelet counts were not reachable. The meta-analysis that pooled this trial required per-group AE counts of each pooled event from every included study: "the study should offer accurate date, including the total number of subjects, the OS, and the number of adverse events of each study group" (PMC6380863, Inclusion criteria), and thrombocytopenia is one of the four pooled events (Fig 3D). The trial's own abstract confirms a graded per-arm AE tabulation exists - "The most common adverse events of grade 3 or worse in the docetaxel, prednisone and custirsen group (n=501) compared with the docetaxel and prednisone alone group (n=499) were neutropenia (grade 3, 63 [13%] vs 28 [6%]; grade 4, 98 [20%] vs 77 [15%]), febrile neutropenia (grade 3, 52 [10%] vs 31 [6%]; grade 4, four [1%] vs two [..." - but the Europe PMC abstract is truncated at that point and no thrombocytopenia figure is visible in it. 'partial', not 'yes': I could not quote a locus in a source I actually reached that states this trial's thrombocytopenia numerator and denominator. The curated rows handle this correctly and TMSR514's grade-1 assignment for epistaxis is the right call - the paper attributes no epistaxis to thrombocytopenia, and BTK inhibition impairs platelet FUNCTION at normal counts, so grading an unattributed bleed as a severe platelet event would manufacture evidence. notes: HEADLINE ANSWER. The 15 curated measurement rows in cluster oncology_aso resolve to 9 EVIDENCE UNITS: 7 registered human trials with verified ClinicalTrials.gov records (NCT00138658, NCT00327340, NCT00054106, NCT03527147, NCT01188187, NCT01578655, NCT00258388), 1 phase 1 healthy-volunteer study for which no registry record could be found (registry_id TBD, not NOT_REGISTERED), and 1 pooled meta-analysis that is NOT a trial. All 15 rows are assigned; none is unassignable. Only 5 of the 9 units carry rows of their own; the other 4 are a pooled analysis and its 3 constituent trials. THE TRIAL COUNT THAT MATTERS: 5 distinct human studies actually generated the 15 platelet measurement rows here - NCT00138658 (4 rows), NCT00327340 (2 rows), NCT00054106 (1 row), the unregistered healthy-volunteer study (1 row), the meta-analysis (1 row) and NCT03527147 module 1 (6 rows) - which is 6 row-bearing units, of which 5 are studies and 1 is a pool. This cluster is therefore the clearest small-scale demonstration of why the dataset's 1002 'human_clinical' rows are not 1002 trials: 6 rows here are six overlapping cells of ONE 17-patient table in ONE paper, and 4 more are four MedDRA views of ONE 81-patient trial. WHY 9 UNITS AND NOT 6. Hard rule 3 permits counting a pooled analysis's constituents only where each is individually identifiable AND independently supported. For PMID 30732140 both conditions are met, so the 3 constituents are instantiated with empty measurement_ids: the article names all three in its reference list ([20] SYNERGY, [21] AFFINITY, [25] Chi 2010 JCO), each resolves to a verified NCT record, and - the decisive check - the pool's stated 857 experimental and 852 control reproduce EXACTLY from the three published safety analysis sets (501+315+41 = 857; 499+312+41 = 852). Their measurement_ids are empty on purpose: no curated row carries any constituent's own platelet data, the pooled odds ratio TMSR511 belongs to the pool, and treating the pool and a constituent as two trial-level platelet observations would double-count 1709 patients. DEDUPLICATION PERFORMED. Four pairs of sources were collapsed to one unit each: NCT00138658 + Laskin 2012 (PMID 22198426); NCT00327340 + Saad 2011 CUOG P-06c (PMID 21788353); NCT00054106 + Chi 2005 JNCI (PMID 16145049) + the Higano 2013 review (PMID 23836992) that is the curated source; NCT03527147 + Roschewski 2023 (PMID 37364001). TWO NON-OVERLAPS WERE VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because both are plausible double-count traps. (1) NCT00327340 is NOT in the meta-analysis: it appears in PMID 30732140 only as Introduction reference [19], while the included studies are [20], [21] and [25] - so TMSR507/TMSR508 share no patient with TMSR511. (2) NCT00258388 (I165, NCIC CTG, n=82, docetaxel/prednisone with or without OGX-011, 41 vs 41, Chi 2010 JCO) and NCT00327340 (OGX-011-07, Achieve/OncoGenex, n=70, custirsen in BOTH arms with the mitoxantrone-or-docetaxel backbone randomised, 23 vs 46, Saad 2011 Clin Cancer Res) are two different randomised phase 2 trials in docetaxel-exposed mCRPC, not one trial reported twice. REGISTRY VERIFICATION. Eight NCT ids are asserted in this file and every one was fetched individually from https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/<NCT> on 2026-10-01 and confirmed to describe the expected compound, phase, condition, sponsor and arm structure: NCT00138658, NCT00327340, NCT00054106, NCT03527147, NCT01188187, NCT01578655, NCT00258388 (asserted as this cluster's trials) plus NCT01874561, fetched only to EXCLUDE it as the healthy-volunteer study. No identifier is asserted anywhere in this file that was not fetched. Two of the eight have posted results (NCT00138658, results first posted 2012-01-10; NCT00327340, 2012-08-29) and in both cases the full adverse-events module was pulled and every curated count re-derived from it, including enumerating all 125 posted AE terms across the two records to confirm which platelet terms are present and which are genuinely absent. The other five have NO posted results, so for those trials every number in this file comes from a publication and is quoted as such. POSTED-RESULTS AUDIT, the question the lead curator asked. Both custirsen trials with posted results DO contain platelet data, but of opposite kinds. NCT00138658 posts four platelet terms with counts (otherEvents 'Platelet Count Decreased' 6/81 under Investigations; otherEvents 'Thrombocytopenia' 25/81 under Blood and lymphatic system disorders; seriousEvents 'Thrombocytopenia' 1/81; seriousEvents 'Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura' 1/81), each flagged assessmentType SYSTEMATIC_ASSESSMENT, with an explicit AE description and a 30-day observation window - the strongest platelet_endpoint_evaluable='yes' basis in the cluster. NCT00327340 posts NO platelet term in either table, which is what the two grade-0 rows rest on. That record is rated 'partial', not 'yes', and the reason is specific: its serious-AE table is a complete tabulation and is populated for both arms, so a zero for SERIOUS platelet events in 23 and in 46 subjects is a real reported zero; but its non-serious table carries frequencyThreshold 5, so absence there establishes only <5%; and unlike NCT00138658 it carries no assessmentType on any event, an empty adverseEventsModule.description and an empty timeFrame, so nothing in it can be quoted as evidence that platelet counts were systematically measured. Per hard rule 5 that caps it at 'partial'. The curated rows are correctly scoped to the serious band, so the rows themselves do not overreach. DEFECTS FOUND IN THE UNDERLYING ROWS (reported, not corrected - this run modified only its own output file). (1) The source_id field is corrupted for 9 of the 15 rows. TMSR503-TMSR511 all carry source_id 'workflow:ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00138658 (posted resul' - a value truncated at 50 characters and then carried forward onto rows whose actual source is a completely different document: TMSR507 and TMSR508 are from NCT00327340, TMSR509 from the Higano 2013 review, TMSR510 from Rabinovich-Guilatt 2015, TMSR511 from the 2019 meta-analysis. Only TMSR512-TMSR517 have a source_id consistent with their own source_ref. source_uid is correct on all 15 rows, so nothing is lost, but source_id must not be used as a join key for rows 503-511. This is the most consequential defect in the cluster. (2) TMSR511 misattributes its source: the row credits 'Liu C, Li K. Medicine (Baltimore). 2019;98(6):e14254', but the Europe PMC authorString for PMID 30732140 is 'Zhang X, Liu C, Li K, Wang K, Zhang Q, Cui Y.' The first author is Zhang X; Liu C and Li K are second and third. PMID, PMCID, DOI, journal, volume, year and e-locator in the row are all correct. (3) TMSR509 has a denominator problem that its fields hide. Its dose is 640 mg, but NCT00054106 treated 25 patients across SIX dose cohorts (40, 80, 160, 320, 480, 640 mg) and the thrombocytopenia statement applies only to 'patients receiving the 640 mg dose', a subcohort whose size is stated nowhere in the Higano review, the Chi 2005 abstract or the registry record. n_analyzed_platelet for that unit is therefore TBD, NOT 25, and any model that reads the row as covering 25 patients is wrong. (4) TMSR503-TMSR506 reproduce a typo from the registry: their exposure_duration says loading doses on 'days -7,-5,3'. The '3' comes from NCT00138658's armsInterventionsModule intervention description; the adverse-events eventGroup description in the same record reads 'Days -7, -5 and -3 of Cycle 1', which is the internally consistent reading. (5) TMSR503-TMSR506 treat 640 mg as the dose, but the 81-patient ITT set is a pooled dose group: 'Most patients received OGX-011 at 640 mg; but 3 patients received a 480 mg dose. The 2 dose groups were combined due to the small number of patients who received 480 mg.' 640 mg is modal, not uniform. (6) AFFINITY's enrolment is inconsistent between sources and is recorded rather than reconciled: registry enrollmentInfo 630 ACTUAL vs the publication's 635 randomised (317 + 318). ONE ROW IMPROVED BY THIS PASS. TMSR510 carries readout_value TBD with a note saying the numeric table could not be retrieved. It can be: the rendered article at PMC4574829 was readable and Table 1 gives 'Activated partial thromboplastin time prolonged' as group A 9 (90) any grade and 6 (60) grade >=2, group B 11 (92) any grade and 1 (8) grade >=2. More importantly for platelet purposes, the Methods establish that platelets were actually measured - 'Laboratory evaluations included complete blood count with differential and coagulation studies (PT/PTT, INR) on day 8 at 0 (pre-dose), 2, 12, 24, 36 and 48 h after the start of the custirsen infusion' - which is why that unit is 'partial' rather than 'no': the platelet endpoint was assessed at six post-dose timepoints at the full 640 mg dose, graded per CTCAE v4.0, and simply never reported. The words 'platelet' and 'thrombocytopenia' do not appear anywhere in that article (0 hits in the full text), so per hard rule 5 no platelet-specific grade-0 row should be created from it, and none is. ATTRIBUTION, read before modelling any row in this cluster. Only ONE of the 15 rows supports a custirsen-attributable platelet effect with a comparator: TMSR511, the pooled thrombocytopenia odds ratio 2.62 (95% CI 1.82-3.77, P<.001), in which both arms of all three constituent trials received the same taxane backbone. Everything else is confounded or uncontrolled. NCT00138658 gave gemcitabine plus cisplatin or carboplatin to every subject with no control arm (and gemcitabine is itself a recognised cause of drug-induced thrombotic microangiopathy, which is the plausible alternative explanation for the one TTP case). NCT00327340 randomised the chemotherapy backbone, not the oligonucleotide, so both arms received custirsen. All six danvatirsen rows come from a cohort in which every patient also took acalabrutinib, a BTK inhibitor with its own platelet and bleeding liability, with no monotherapy arm. The cleanest oligonucleotide-attributable platelet signal in the cluster is therefore the weakest-quantified one: NCT00054106, where custirsen was given with buserelin, flutamide and surgery and NO cytotoxic chemotherapy, and thrombocytopenia was among the most frequent AEs at 640 mg - but with all toxicities capped at grade 1/2, no incidence figure and no stated denominator. NON-SUMMATION WARNINGS. Within NCT03527147 module 1, all six rows share the single denominator of 17 and are overlapping views of it: 'Platelet count decreased' any grade 8/17 contains its grade >=3 subset 4/17; 'Thrombocytopenia' any grade 3/17 contains its grade >=3 subset 2/17; those two MedDRA preferred terms have unresolved patient-level overlap, so the true platelet-affected fraction lies between 47% and 65%; and the single discontinuation for platelet count decreased is very probably one of the four grade >=3 platelet-count-decreased patients. Within NCT00138658, the four rows are four MedDRA views of the same 81 patients. Across units, the pool's 1709 already contains SYNERGY's 1000, AFFINITY's 627 and Chi 2010's 82. And the registry's enrolment counts are not the platelet denominators anywhere in this cluster: 85 vs 81 for NCT00138658, 70 vs 23 and 46 for NCT00327340, 30 (whole platform) vs 17 (module 1) for NCT03527147, 25 vs an unstated 640 mg subcohort for NCT00054106. LIMITATIONS. Five documents could not be read and nothing was inferred from them: Chi KN et al. J Natl Cancer Inst 2005;97:1287-96 (closed access, no PMCID) so the per-dose toxicity table of NCT00054106 and the size of its 640 mg cohort are unknown; Chi KN et al. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:473-85 (SYNERGY) and Beer TM et al. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1532-42 (AFFINITY), both paywalled with no PMCID and no posted registry results, so neither trial's own per-arm thrombocytopenia counts were seen; Chi KN et al. J Clin Oncol 2010;28:4247-54, likewise paywalled, whose abstract mentions no platelet endpoint at all. Figure 3D of PMID 30732140, which carries the per-trial thrombocytopenia event counts behind the pooled OR, is a raster image and was not read. That is why all three constituents are platelet_endpoint_evaluable 'partial' and confidence 'medium' rather than 'yes'/'high'. Europe PMC does not serve fullTextXML for PMC4574829, so that article was read from its rendered PMC page instead. No EMA or FDA document was consulted: neither custirsen nor danvatirsen was ever approved, so no EPAR or label exists for either compound, and the cluster contains no label-derived row.
